chunks: And We did not send into any city a prophet except that We seized its people with adversity and hardship, so that they might submit.

key_terms.يَضَّرَّعُونَ: they may submit or supplicate humbly

ai.seo_question: Why does God send prophets with trials and hardship for their people?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the pedagogical purpose of divine afflictions (bala') as a means to awaken spiritual consciousness and induce *tadarru'* (humble supplication) among the people. It underscores that hardship is not merely punitive but serves as a catalyst for returning to God, a concept deeply linked to the Imams' teachings on the wisdom behind trials. This methodology reflects the balance between divine mercy and the necessity of human responsiveness to guidance.
